key_findings: Intrathecal K252a (TrkB inhibitor) reduced mechanical hyperalgesia and cold allodynia after brachial plexus avulsion in rats.
K252a decreased spinal BDNF, TrkB and GFAP and increased KCC2 expression in the C5-T1 dorsal horn, implicating the BDNF-TrkB-KCC2 pathway in BPA neuropathic pain.
